title: The digest verifier is handed a hash of the password as the expected secret, so the stored hash is the credential
index_line: T-0077 · AUTH_DECISION · WS-Security PasswordDigest against a server that hashes its own password: the hash is the credential · dotnet · corroborated
invariant_violated: The staging service assumed that passing a SHA1 of the configured password to the WS-Security digest verifier was the same as passing the password; but the client's digest is computed over whatever secret the server names, so the check proves knowledge of the hash, not of the plaintext.

mechanism.does: a SOAP request to /CMSPages/Staging/SyncServer.asmx carries a WS-Security UsernameToken whose Password Type attribute is chosen by the client
WSE3 reads the attacker-supplied Type attribute and routes verification to VerifyHashedPassword instead of VerifyPlainTextPassword
Kentico's overridden AuthenticateToken returns GetSHA1Hash(configuredPassword) as the expected secret for the named user
VerifyHashedPassword computes SHA1(nonce + created + expectedSecret) and compares it with the digest in the request
because the expected secret is itself a hash, the attacker computes the digest over the hash — possession of the stored hash is sufficient and the password is never needed
the token is marked authenticated and the staging task data is accepted for deserialization, which is the code-execution surface

source.http.body.value: the SOAP envelope: both the UsernameToken Password Type and the staging task payload are attacker-controlled XML

guard.signature.value: the WS-Security digest check, defeated because the verifier's own 'expected secret' is a hash of the password

sink.deser.native.value: the staging endpoint deserializes stagingTaskData with SoapFormatter once the token is accepted

encoding.string.value: PasswordDigest = Base64(SHA1(nonce + created + secret)) — the encoding that makes the hash usable as a credential

preconditions.expr: the staging SOAP endpoint is reachable
the build overrides UsernameTokenManager and hashes the stored password before handing it to the verifier
the Staging service is enabled with user-name/password authentication (X.509 mode is not affected)

check.spec: curl -s -X POST http://HOST/CMSPages/Staging/SyncServer.asmx -H 'Content-Type: text/xml' --data '<soap:Envelope xmlns:soap="http://schemas.xmlsoap.org/soap/envelope/"><soap:Body><ProcessSynchronizationTaskData xmlns="http://localhost/SyncWebService/SyncServer"><stagingTaskData>x</stagingTaskData></ProcessSynchronizationTaskData></soap:Body></soap:Envelope>' | grep -i 'missing username token\|invalid security token'

success: a PasswordDigest built from the SHA1 of the configured password is accepted where the plaintext was never known
the SOAP action proceeds past authentication into staging-task processing
failure_like: the endpoint demands X.509 client certificates
the server hashes with a salt/iteration the client cannot reproduce, so the digest does not validate
false_positive: a fault mentioning 'invalid security token' means the digest path ran — it is not a bypass
a username mismatch returns an empty expected secret and is rejected; only a matching user name exercises the flaw

hazards: any custom password-verification hook that pre-hashes the stored secret before the library compares it
WS-Security/WSE-style stacks where the client picks the password type in the message
hash-as-credential generalises to pass-the-hash against any verifier that compares hashes
non_transfers: verifiers that compute a salted KDF from the plaintext inside the comparison
protocols where the password type is fixed by configuration, not chosen in the message

evidence.target: Kentico Xperience <= 13.0.178, Staging/Sync Server SyncServer.asmx with user-name/password authentication (CVE-2025-2746)

provenance.author: watchTowr Labs
provenance.corroborates: CVE-2025-2746: Kentico overrides UsernameTokenManager.AuthenticateToken and returns StagingTaskRunner.GetSHA1Hash(configuredPassword) as the expected secret; the client may set Password Type=PasswordDigest, so the digest can be computed over the hash without knowing the plaintext — full source snippets and a working request
